name: Massing energy indicators (VFAR, WWR, orientation, thermal bridging)
question: How compact, glazed and oriented is my massing, and what does that imply for heating demand (TEDI) before any simulation is run?
method: 1) Slice the mesh per storey; classify exterior faces by normal tilt (default 10 degrees) into walls and roof. 2) Rotate normals by the true-north offset and bin into 8 azimuth sectors. 3) MFA = tagged floor area (parkade excluded); VFAR = above-ground wall area / MFA; plate depth = longest facade-to-core distance. 4) Glazing = WWR preset x wall area. 5) Effective U = clear-field U plus psi x length bridging per storey (BETBG-style presets, team assumption). 6) TEDI proxy band = [UA_eff x HDD x 24/1000 + ventilation loss x (1 - SRE) + infiltration loss - usable gains] / MFA, HDD from the EPW;…
human: Facade composition, glazing versus views, daylight and cultural expression; whether higher WWR is justified by human-scale and City in Nature intent; shading, fin and balcony strategy.
limits: Screening proxy only: no thermal mass, HVAC or stack model. Bridging presets, orientation and plate-depth magnitudes are unsourced. Relative indicators depend on the reference box. Not a compliance calculation.
